requirement: Yield checks and quantity reconciliations are to be performed as needed to show there are no discrepancies beyond acceptable limits; any significant departure from the expected yield must be recorded and investigated.
system_implications: Master defines yield/reconciliation checkpoints with theoretical basis, formula and alert/action limits. At each checkpoint the system calculates the result from captured quantities (inputs, outputs, samples, rejects, waste, residues) and blocks progression past a hard limit until a deviation is opened, linked and (as configured) approved. Results within limits are recorded; out-of-limit results appear in the exception report and hold batch disposition. Tablets: granule yield after drying/milling, compressed tablet count vs. theoretical, coating weight gain. Injectables: compounded volume vs. theoretical, filled units vs. theoretical, lyophilised vials, visual-inspection rejects.
verification_test: Enter quantities that produce a yield below the action limit: system forces deviation creation before the next step and flags the batch; a yield inside limits proceeds without deviation. Recalculation from raw quantities matches the displayed yield.

requirement: Before a processing operation starts, it must be confirmed that the area and equipment are clean and hold no materials, products, residues or paperwork unrelated to the operation about to begin.
system_implications: Mandatory processing-area clearance step at the start of each processing stage (and after interruptions/changeovers) using a master-defined checklist; the system verifies electronically what it can (previous batch closed in the room/equipment logbook, equipment clean status and clean-hold time valid, no open material lots assigned to the room) and requires signed confirmation of physical checks. Configurable independent verification by a second person. Stage cannot start until clearance is signed.
verification_test: Attempt to start granulation/compounding while the room logbook shows the prior batch not cleared or equipment clean-hold expired -> blocked. After signed clearance (and verifier signature if configured), the step unlocks and both signatures appear in the batch record.

requirement: Different products may only be handled in the same room at the same time, or back-to-back, if this has been shown to create no risk of mix-up or cross-contamination.
system_implications: Room/area occupancy control: the system tracks which batch/product occupies each room and refuses to start a second product in a room already occupied, unless the room is configured (under QA approval) as segregated for concurrent work with a documented risk assessment reference. Consecutive product use requires completed cleaning and clearance before the room status returns to available.
verification_test: Start batch A (product X) in room R; attempt to start batch B (product Y) in room R -> blocked with message. After batch A closes and cleaning + clearance are recorded, batch B can start.

requirement: During processing, every material, bulk container, major equipment item and, where appropriate, room must carry a label or other identification showing the product or material, strength where relevant, batch number and, where applicable, the production stage. Labels must be unambiguous, easy to read and follow the company's standard layout; colours signalling status (such as quarantine, approved, rejected or cleaned) are recommended as an extra aid.
system_implications: System generates and prints status/identity labels from batch data in approved templates (product, strength, batch, stage, container n of N, gross/tare/net, status, date/time, user) with a barcode/2D code; room and equipment status displays (e.g. 'In use - product/batch/stage', 'Cleaned - valid until', 'To be cleaned'). Scanning of container and equipment labels at each step verifies identity and status, replacing reliance on visual checks. Status changes (quarantine -> released -> rejected) update electronic status and require relabel/reprint with audit trail.
verification_test: Weigh a material into a container: label shows all required fields and a scannable code. Scan a container labelled for a different batch or stage at the next step -> rejected. Equipment status screen changes from 'In use' to 'To be cleaned' at batch end.

requirement: Deviating from instructions or procedures is to be kept to a minimum; when a deviation does happen, a competent person must give written approval, with Quality Control involved when relevant.
system_implications: Recipe enforcement prevents undocumented departures (sequence, limits, material identity). Any intentional departure (e.g. parameter outside range, step skipped, alternative equipment) is only possible through an in-line deviation/exception form that captures description and impact and requires e-signature approval by a role flagged as competent for that deviation class; QA/QC approval is mandatory for classes configured as quality-impacting. Deviation ID is linked to the step and appears in the batch record and exception report; batch release is blocked while linked deviations are open.
verification_test: Try to skip a mandatory step -> blocked unless a deviation is raised and approved by an authorised role. Operator cannot self-approve. Release blocked with an open deviation.

requirement: Dispensing of starting materials is restricted to designated staff working to a written procedure, so that the right material in the right quantity ends up in clean, correctly labelled containers. An independent second check of each dispensed item and its quantity is required and must be documented. Everything dispensed for one batch is kept as a group and visibly labelled as belonging to that batch.
system_implications: Dispensing module: user must hold the 'dispenser' qualification (training record current) to log in to the booth; material lot scanned and checked against BOM, released status and retest/expiry date; weight captured directly from a calibrated, daily-checked balance with tolerance check against target; container label printed automatically. Independent check is either a second person e-signature (different user) or a validated system check (barcode + balance interface) documented as equivalent. Dispensed items grouped into a batch 'kit' with kit label and completeness check before issue to production. Injectables: also dispensing of WFI volumes, pH adjusters, filter/stopper components; tablets: API potency-adjusted quantities with compensating excipient.
verification_test: Log in without dispenser qualification -> refused. Scan wrong lot or a quarantined/expired lot -> refused. Weight outside tolerance cannot be confirmed. Verifier cannot be the dispenser. Kit cannot be issued with a missing component.

requirement: Cross-contamination must be prevented using quality risk management informed by toxicological assessment (health-based exposure limits); the QRM outcome decides whether premises/equipment must be dedicated and how extensive the technical measures (e.g. dedicated or self-contained areas, closed systems, barriers, validated cleaning) and organisational measures (e.g. campaigns, dedicated gowning, cleaning verification, status records) must be; the measures and their effectiveness are reviewed periodically. Non-medicinal products are normally kept out of medicinal production areas.
system_implications: Product master carries cross-contamination attributes (HBEL/PDE class, dedicated-equipment flag, allowed equipment/rooms, campaign rules, required cleaning procedure and verification type). Scheduler and execution enforce them: only permitted equipment/rooms selectable; campaign length and between-product cleaning type enforced; cleaning verification result (e.g. swab/rinse pass) must be recorded before a different product can use the equipment. Changeover matrix (product A -> product B) drives required cleaning level. Periodic review report of cleaning failures and changeovers.
verification_test: Assign a highly potent product to non-dedicated equipment not in its allowed list -> blocked. Attempt to start product B on equipment after product A with only a minor clean when the matrix requires full clean + verification -> blocked. Campaign exceeding configured maximum batches -> blocked or deviation required.

requirement: Packaging programmes must be planned to minimise risks of cross-contamination, mix-up or substitution; different products are not packaged close to each other unless physically segregated. The product name and batch number being packed must be displayed at every packaging station or line.
system_implications: Line/room model with segregation attributes; scheduler/execution refuses to start a second product on an adjacent line flagged as not physically segregated. Each line has an electronic line-status display (HMI/terminal/screen) driven by the active packaging order showing product, strength, pack, batch number and status; the display clears only when the order is closed and line clearance is done.
verification_test: Start product X on line 1; attempt product Y on non-segregated line 2 in the same room -> blocked. Line display shows current product/batch and reverts to 'awaiting clearance' at order close.

requirement: Before packaging starts, the work area, packaging lines, printers and other equipment must be verified clean and free of any product, material or document from earlier work that is not needed now; this line clearance follows an appropriate checklist.
system_implications: Packaging order has a mandatory first step 'line clearance' with a master-defined, line-specific checklist (each item individually confirmed, e.g. feeder hoppers, reject bins, printer ribbons/plates, vision-system recipe, floor/under-machine areas, documents removed). Design choice (not mandated by the text, but common inspector expectation for mix-up risk): performer + independent verifier signatures by two different users, verifier typically QA or supervisor. The system also checks electronically that the previous order on that line is closed and reconciled and that no components of another order remain allocated to the line. No packaging step, printer job or line start can be released until clearance is signed.
verification_test: Attempt to start the first packaging step with clearance unsigned or only single-signed (when dual is configured) -> blocked. Same user signing as performer and verifier -> refused. Previous order on the line not closed -> clearance cannot be completed.

requirement: On arrival at the packaging area, every product and packaging component must be checked to confirm the right quantity, the right identity and agreement with the packaging instructions.
system_implications: Receipt-at-line step: scan each bulk container and packaging component lot; system checks item code and artwork/version against the packaging master BOM, released status, expiry, and issued quantity vs. required quantity; mismatches block the step. Quantities received are posted to the reconciliation ledger for the order.
verification_test: Scan a carton of the wrong artwork version or a leaflet for another market -> rejected. Scan a quarantined component lot -> rejected. Received quantity feeds reconciliation.

requirement: Containers must be cleaned before they are filled, with particular care to prevent or remove foreign matter such as glass or metal particles. Labelling should normally follow filling and closing without delay; where it does not, procedures must prevent mix-ups and wrong labelling.
system_implications: Injectables edition (primary relevance): record container washing/depyrogenation and sterilisation status for each lot of vials/ampoules/stoppers with hold-time limits; unlabelled filled units (e.g. held for inspection before labelling) are tracked as 'bright stock' with unique tray/container IDs, location, count and hold-time; labelling order can only consume bright stock of the matching batch, verified by scan. Tablets edition: bottle cleaning/air-rinse and foreign-matter checks; bulk tablets in unlabelled containers carry system-printed identity labels. Maximum interval between filling and labelling configurable with alert.
verification_test: Attempt to label bright-stock trays from batch A under order for batch B -> rejected. Bright stock exceeding maximum unlabelled hold time raises an exception. Filling step blocked if container depyrogenation/sterile hold time has expired (injectables).

requirement: Printed components need special care: secure storage with access limited to authorised people; loose items such as cut labels kept and moved in closed, separate containers; and issue to production only by authorised staff following an approved written procedure. Each incoming lot of printed or primary packaging material is assigned its own reference number or identification mark. Primary or printed packaging that is out of date or obsolete must be destroyed, with the disposal documented.
system_implications: Packaging-material issue transaction restricted to an authorised role; each issued unit (reel, carton bundle, sealed box of cut labels) scanned by its internal lot/reference number and linked to the packaging order; closed-container ID recorded for cut labels. Artwork version lifecycle: when an artwork is superseded, all stock lots of the old version are automatically blocked for issue and routed to a destruction task requiring recorded, witnessed disposal.
verification_test: Non-authorised user attempts to issue labels -> refused. Issue of a lot whose artwork version is obsolete -> blocked. Destruction task for obsolete stock requires quantities, method, date and signatures and closes the lot.

requirement: Correct execution of every printing operation (e.g. batch code, expiry date), whether done separately or during packaging, must be checked and recorded, and any hand printing re-checked at regular intervals. Extra care is required with cut labels and with off-line overprinting; roll-fed labels are normally preferred over cut labels to help avoid mix-ups.
system_implications: Variable print data (batch, expiry, MFG date, serial/2D code, price where applicable) is sent electronically from the batch record to printers/coders (no manual keying); expiry is calculated from the master shelf-life rule. Start-of-run and periodic print verification step: operator/vision system confirms printed text against expected values; results recorded with specimen image. Configurable recurring re-check interval for any manual/hand printing. Master flags cut-label usage and off-line overprinting as higher-risk operations requiring additional controls (e.g. 100% vision check, dual verification).
verification_test: Batch data change after print setup -> printer job invalidated until re-verified. Start-up print check missing -> line cannot go to production mode. Hand-print re-check overdue -> alarm and exception entry.

requirement: The correct operation of electronic code readers, label counters and comparable devices must be checked. Printed or embossed information on packs must be clear and must not easily fade or rub off.
system_implications: Device challenge tests defined in the master (e.g. deliberately present wrong-code, missing-label, unreadable-code and missing-leaflet test pieces) at start-up, after interventions/stoppages, and at end of run; each challenge result is recorded (pass/fail, who, when) and a failed or missing challenge blocks production mode. Challenge test pieces are counted out and back in. Print quality check (grade for 2D codes where applicable, legibility, smudge/rub resistance per specification) recorded as an IPC.
verification_test: Skip the start-up challenge -> line cannot run in production mode. Record a failed challenge -> line stopped and deviation required. Challenge pieces not all returned at end -> reconciliation exception.

requirement: During packaging, on-line checks must at least confirm that finished packs look right and are complete, that the correct product and components are being used and any overprint is right, and that line monitoring devices are working. Units taken off the line as samples must never be put back.
system_implications: IPC plan in packaging master contains (as a minimum) these check categories at defined frequency with pass/fail and sample counts; missed IPCs raise alerts. Samples withdrawn are recorded by quantity and purpose and are automatically deducted in reconciliation; the system provides no transaction to return sampled units to the line. Injectables: also container-closure checks (crimp/seal), label placement on vials; tablets: blister seal integrity/leak test, count per bottle.
verification_test: IPC not recorded within its interval -> alert and exception report entry. Attempt to add sampled units back to good output -> not possible. Reconciliation shows sample quantities as a separate line.

requirement: If product is caught up in an unusual event (e.g. jam, spill, dropped units, suspected mix-up), it may re-enter the process only after it has been specially inspected, the event investigated, and authorised staff have approved; this must be documented in detail.
system_implications: 'Set-aside/unusual event' transaction: affected units are counted and moved to a quarantined set-aside bucket linked to an event record (what happened, time, quantity, location). Reintroduction requires inspection result entry, investigation reference and approval e-signature by an authorised role (not the operator); otherwise units go to reject. All quantities flow into reconciliation.
verification_test: Record a jam with 40 units set aside; attempt to add them back to good output without approval -> blocked. With inspection + approval, reintroduced quantity appears in the record and reconciliation with the event ID.

requirement: Any significant or unusual discrepancy found when reconciling bulk quantity and printed packaging materials against units produced must be investigated and satisfactorily explained before the batch is released.
system_implications: End-of-order reconciliation computed automatically per bulk lot and per printed component: issued = used + destroyed + returned + samples + rejects (+ set-aside), with master-defined limits (tighter, often zero-tolerance, for batch-coded printed items). Result outside limits forces a linked deviation/investigation; the order cannot be closed and the batch cannot be certified until the investigation is closed and approved by QA. Tablets: bulk tablets by weight/count vs. packs produced; injectables: filled/inspected units vs. labelled units vs. cartons.
verification_test: Enter counts leaving 12 labels unaccounted with a zero-tolerance limit -> order close blocked, deviation required; QP certification blocked until deviation closed. Counts within limits -> order closes normally.

requirement: When packaging is finished, any unused packaging material already coded with the batch must be destroyed and the destruction recorded; returning uncoded printed materials to stock must follow a documented procedure.
system_implications: Order close-out wizard: system distinguishes coded vs. uncoded leftovers (based on whether in-line/off-line coding occurred). Coded leftovers must be entered on a destruction record (quantity, method, witness) and can never be returned to stock; uncoded leftovers go through a return-to-stock transaction with count verification, re-labelling of the container and QA/stores acceptance, updating the component lot quantity.
verification_test: Attempt to return batch-coded cartons to stock -> no transaction available. Uncoded label return requires counted quantity, verification signature and updates stock. Destruction quantities appear in the reconciliation.

requirement: Necessary in-process and environmental controls must be performed and recorded, and intermediate and bulk products must be held under appropriate conditions.
system_implications: IPCs scheduled by the master (frequency, sample size, limits) with automatic data capture from instruments where possible (balances, hardness/thickness testers, checkweighers, fill-weight systems, pH/conductivity meters); out-of-limit results trigger defined reactions. Environmental data for the room during the step (e.g. temperature/RH for hygroscopic tablets; for injectables grade A/B particle counts, viable monitoring results, differential pressures) are linked to the batch record by time window from the monitoring system, and excursions are pulled into the exception report. Bulk/intermediate holds record container, location, storage condition and hold start/stop, with maximum hold time checks.
verification_test: Miss a scheduled IPC -> alert and exception. Inject an EM excursion during the filling window -> appears in batch exception report and blocks QA review completion until assessed. Bulk hold exceeding validated time -> blocked or deviation required.

requirement: Rejected materials and products must be clearly marked as rejected and segregated in restricted-access storage. Their fate (return to supplier, reprocessing where appropriate, or destruction) must be approved and documented by authorised people.
system_implications: 'Rejected' is a hard system status that blocks every consumption, issue, packaging and shipping transaction; rejected stock must be moved to a restricted location type. Disposition workflow (return to supplier / reprocess / destroy) with authorised-role approval e-signature and a record of the executed action and quantities. In-process rejects (e.g. tablets rejected by checkweigher, vials rejected at visual inspection) are counted into reject containers with IDs and follow the same disposition path.
verification_test: Try to dispense or package a rejected lot -> blocked. Attempt to move rejected stock to a normal location -> blocked. Disposition without authorised approval -> blocked; completed disposition visible in lot history.

requirement: Reprocessing of rejected product is to be exceptional: allowed only when final quality is unaffected, specifications are met, and it follows a defined, authorised procedure after risk evaluation; a record of the reprocessing must be kept.
system_implications: Reprocessing can only be executed from a pre-approved reprocessing master/procedure linked to the product (never ad hoc), launched from an approved deviation/change record with documented risk assessment. The reprocessing record is generated like a batch record, linked to the original batch genealogy, and flagged so QA/QP see it at release; additional testing requirements from the procedure are enforced. Injectables: reprocessing is often not permitted for sterile products (e.g. re-filtration only if validated/registered) - system allows reprocessing masters to be disabled per product.
verification_test: Attempt to start reprocessing without an approved reprocessing procedure and approved risk assessment -> blocked. Completed reprocessing appears in the original batch genealogy and QP review flags.

requirement: Adding all or part of earlier batches that meet quality requirements into a later batch of the same product, at a defined manufacturing stage, needs prior authorisation, must follow a defined procedure after assessing risks (including any effect on shelf life), and must be recorded. QC must decide whether reprocessed product, or product containing recovered material, needs extra testing.
system_implications: Recovered-material addition is a specific step type available only where the master defines it (stage, maximum proportion, eligible source batches). Source batch must be same product, conforming status and within age limits; pre-authorisation e-signature required; genealogy records source batch IDs and quantities; expiry of the receiving batch is calculated from the oldest contributing batch where the procedure requires. QC additional-testing decision is captured as a mandatory field before release.
verification_test: Try to add material from a different product or a non-conforming batch -> blocked. Add eligible recovered material: pre-authorisation required, genealogy and expiry calculation updated, QC decision field mandatory before release.

requirement: Market returns that have been outside the manufacturer's control default to destruction unless their quality is not in doubt. Resale, relabelling or use in a later batch is allowed only after QC has critically assessed them under a written procedure, considering the product type, any special storage needs, its condition and history, and how long it has been out. If quality is doubtful the goods must not be reissued or reused (though basic chemical recovery of the active substance may be possible). All actions must be recorded.
system_implications: Returned-goods receipt creates a quarantined 'returned' lot linked to the original batch; disposition requires a QC assessment form (storage history incl. cold chain for injectables, condition, time since shipment) and QC e-signature; default disposition is destroy. Returned units cannot be consumed as recovered material or repackaged unless the assessment result permits it, and the resulting action is recorded against the original batch history.
verification_test: Try to repackage returned units without a QC assessment -> blocked. Assessment 'doubt' -> only destruction (or chemical recovery route) available.

requirement: Finished products stay in quarantine, under manufacturer-defined conditions, until final release (evaluation per Chapter 6 and QP certification); only after release do they become usable stock. Incoming materials and products are likewise held in physical or administrative quarantine until released.
system_implications: Every produced lot is created in 'Quarantine' status; status change to 'Released' is possible only via the QP certification transaction after batch record review is complete (all steps signed, deviations closed, reconciliation passed, lab results approved). Interfaces to ERP/WMS must respect the status (no shipment of quarantined stock). Administrative quarantine is acceptable if enforced electronically.
verification_test: Attempt to ship or allocate a quarantined finished lot via ERP interface -> rejected. QP certification button disabled while any release prerequisite is open. Status history shows who released and when.

requirement: Products and materials need protection against microbial and other contamination throughout processing; handling of dry materials requires special measures to stop dust being generated and spread, especially for highly hazardous or sensitising substances.
system_implications: Tablets edition: master can require dust-control prerequisites before open handling steps (e.g. local exhaust/containment verified on, room pressure cascade OK, contained transfer system connected) captured as signed checks or interface signals; weighing/dispensing of potent APIs only in designated booths. Injectables edition: aseptic-processing prerequisites before exposure steps (grade A airflow/particle status OK, sterile equipment within hold time, gowning qualification valid, interventions logged); microbial hold-time limits for non-sterile bulk solution before sterile filtration (bioburden sample recorded).
verification_test: Attempt to start an open-powder step while the containment/extraction check is not recorded -> blocked (tablets). Attempt to start filling with sterile-hold expired on filling parts or with an active grade A alarm -> blocked (injectables). Bulk solution time from compounding start to filtration exceeding limit -> deviation required.

requirement: Checks must confirm that pipelines and other equipment that transfer product from one area to another are correctly connected.
system_implications: Transfer steps (e.g. bulk solution from compounding vessel to filling line through transfer panel/hoses; vacuum/pneumatic powder transfer to tablet press hopper) include a connection-verification step: scan of source vessel, transfer panel/hose/port and destination IDs, or signal from panel proximity sensors, compared to the master route; mismatch blocks the transfer. Result recorded with performer and verifier.
verification_test: Scan a hose connected to the wrong destination vessel -> transfer blocked. Correct route scan -> transfer enabled and recorded.

requirement: Storage labels on starting materials must identify the material and its receipt lot, and show QC status and any expiry or retest date where relevant; with a fully computerised storage system this may be held electronically instead of legibly on the label. Measures must assure the identity of the contents of every container, and only materials released by QC and still within their retest date may be used.
system_implications: eBMR relies on (or provides) a validated inventory status as the master for material status; at dispensing and at charging into equipment, each container scan checks identity (item code), released status, retest/expiry date, and container-level identity confirmation where required (e.g. per-container ID test status). If labels carry only a barcode, the system is the authoritative source and must be validated for that purpose.
verification_test: Scan a container whose lot is 'on test', rejected, past retest date, or whose container identity test is pending -> blocked at dispensing and at charging. Released, in-date container -> accepted.

requirement: Production must be carried out and overseen by competent staff, and every handling activity for materials and products, from goods receipt through processing and packaging to distribution, must follow written procedures or instructions and be recorded where necessary.
system_implications: Each master step declares the qualification/training required (per procedure version); the system checks the user's current training status (from LMS interface or internal records) before allowing them to perform or verify the step, and blocks users whose training is missing or expired. Supervisor/verifier roles are distinct permissions. Each step links to the governing procedure/instruction version.
verification_test: User trained on SOP v3 attempts a step now requiring SOP v4 training -> refused. Qualified user can perform; verifier role cannot be assigned to an untrained user.

requirement: New formulas or methods of preparation must be shown suitable for routine production, significant changes to the process (including equipment or material changes) that may affect quality or reproducibility must be validated, and processes are periodically reassessed; validation results are recorded.
system_implications: Master recipe change control: every master change is classified (editorial vs. process-impacting); process-impacting changes (CPP ranges, equipment class, materials/suppliers, batch size, sequence) require a linked change-control and validation reference before approval. Masters carry a validation-status attribute; batches produced under a master pending validation (e.g. PPQ batches) are flagged so release requires the validation outcome. Master comparison report (diff) supports the assessment.
verification_test: Attempt to approve a master revision with a changed CPP range and no change-control/validation link -> blocked. Diff report lists changed fields. PPQ-flagged batch cannot be certified without validation outcome entry.

requirement: The manufacturer must promptly tell the marketing authorisation holder about manufacturing constraints that could cause an abnormal restriction of supply, so the MAH can notify the competent authorities.
system_implications: Peripheral to the batch record but can be supported: batch/campaign rejection, prolonged line holds, or major deviations flagged with a 'potential supply impact' attribute that generates a notification task to the supply/QA contact for the MAH, with timestamped acknowledgement.
verification_test: Reject a batch flagged 'supply impact' -> notification task created with due date and audit trail of acknowledgement.
